text:
maria: quick heads-up — running int6 onboarding for safari-embed-v2 on longtail-2026 and seeing a weird semantic collapse for rare synonyms. recall@1 down ~8% vs float32. examples: 'soda' and 'pop' neighbors identical, but should be near but distinct. anyone seen this after per-channel int6? :thinking:
alex: can you paste the eval command + a tiny output snippet? also which quant lib (onnx/ggml/custom)?
maria: eval command below. produced numbers and a small neighbor dump.
```
run_eval --model safari-embed-v2 --quant int6-perchannel --dataset longtail-2026 --metrics recall@1,recall@5,silhouette --distance cosine --seed 42
```
maria: results: recall@1 float32=0.74 -> int6=0.66, recall@5 0.92 -> 0.90, silhouette float32=0.41 -> int6=0.27. sample neighbors for query 'soda': 1) 'soda' (self) 2) 'coke' 3) 'pop' (rank 3 but embedding dot almost same as 'coke')
cheng: hmm. two quick checks: 1) are you L2-norming before quant? 2) are you using cosine vs angular? quant errors can collapse small-angle diffs.
maria: norm before quant yes. cosine metric used.
annika: try per-channel asymmetric quant + clamp using 99.9th percentile stats. per-tensor int6 tends to squash tails. also try calibrating with a small representative subset (longtail 5k).
alex: also compare using angular distance (arccos of dot) — sometimes rank order more robust. and try reranking top-10 with a cross-encoder if latency allows (fallback).
ops-bot: perf-run scheduled: safari-embed-v2-int6-perchannel calibration job queued (job id: pr-4821). ETA ~12m. :gear:
maria: dump of neighbor distances (float vs int6) for two queries: 'soda' float d-to-pop=0.12, d-to-coke=0.09; int6 d-to-pop=0.03, d-to-coke=0.029 (differences under float rounding). looks like quant noise collapsing the micro-diff.
cheng: can you share histogram of quantized scales per-channel? if some channels have tiny scale, tiny deltas get rounded to same bucket. also check dtype saturation/clamping.
maria: attaching quick stats inline: channel_scale median=0.018, 95p=0.072, min=0.0009. a few channels tiny.
annika: that min=0.0009 is suspect. maybe per-channel stats computed on a small batch. use larger calibration set or percentile clipping. also try asymmetric zero-point so small offsets preserved.
alex: another idea — switch to 6-bit + 2-bit residual (mixed precision) for top-k dims (the 'top-k quant residual' trick). more complex but preserves fine-grained neighbors.
maria: ops-bot job ran and posted quick numbers: recall@1 int6-perchannel-clamped=0.71 (was 0.66), recall@5=0.905, silhouette=0.33. improvement but still ~3% behind float. posting full run next.
cheng: nice. that suggests calibration/clamp helped. remaining gap could be due to representation capacity loss — test int5? probably worse.
annika: plan: 1) rerun with larger calibration sample (50k) + 99.9p clamp 2) try asymmetric zero-point 3) test angular vs cosine 4) evaluate cross-encoder rerank on top-10 for recall@1 recovery.
maria: I'll run 1+2 and post results. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
alex: if you want, I can prototype a tiny residual-correction pipeline for top-64 dims tomorrow.
maria: please do — file a tiny RFC and we'll A/B it on a small customer cohort.
ops-bot: note: escalation ticket auto-created for model-onboard-4821 due to >5% recall regression on longtail cohort.
maria: ack. updating ticket with calibration logs and neighbor dumps. will report back in this thread when we have the 50k calibration run outputs.
